title: Lesson 76: Cost Architecture: Licensing, API Consumption, Storage, and Optimization
description: The four cost meters in a Salesforce design, how each one is calculated, and which optimization moves actually change the run rate.

questions.question: Which principle should guide an architect who wants to lower API consumption for a nightly data load?
options: Cost scales with record count, so splitting the load into more calls lowers the bill.
Cost scales with named users, so only seat count changes consumption.
Cost scales with the call, so batching records into fewer calls lowers the bill.
Cost scales with storage volume, so only archiving changes consumption.
questions.explanation: The unit of cost is the call, not the record; a bulk job or composite request carries many records per call, which is why it costs far less than one call per record.

questions.question: A support agent carries a large pasted context on every turn. Why does trimming that context cut the AI bill by whole multiples?
options: Billing rounds prompt size up in fixed token blocks, so crossing a block boundary drops whole units.
Billing charges only for output tokens, so shorter input context has no effect on cost.
Billing multiplies by the number of actions, so context size changes the action count.
Billing charges the context once per conversation, so trimming it has no effect on the recurring bill.
questions.explanation: Prompt billing is per block of up to 2,000 tokens rounded up, so a smaller context can cross a block boundary and bill one unit instead of several.

questions.question: A large group of users only reads cases and updates one status field. Which licensing approach fits that usage?
options: Buy the top license tier for everyone, because a lower tier blocks all record updates and reports.
Use a lower base license and grant the few extra capabilities with permission set licenses.
Use community licenses for internal staff, because they carry the same feature ceiling.
Skip permission sets and widen the profile, because permission sets cannot grant features.
questions.explanation: The base license sets the ceiling and permission set licenses raise it for specific people, so read-mostly users do not need a full seat to get the few capabilities they use.
